nameStory: This delicate wildflower earned its "blue-eyed mary" name from its charming two-toned flowers that look like tiny blue and white eyes peering up from the forest floor. The "small-flowered" part distinguishes it from its showier relatives - this modest Mary keeps her blooms petite and understated, rarely larger than a pencil eraser.
description: Small-flowered blue-eyed mary is a tiny annual wildflower that grows just 2-6 inches tall in delicate, branching clusters. Its most distinctive feature is its miniature two-toned flowers - white on top and blue or purple on the bottom - that bloom in small clusters along slender stems. The plant has small, oval leaves arranged in pairs along the stem and creates carpets of dainty blooms in suitable habitat. Despite its small stature, this hardy little wildflower can form impressive colonies when conditions are right.

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Tiny tubular flowers split into two lips - the upper lip is white or pale, the lower lip is blue, purple, or lavender, creating a distinctive two-toned appearance that looks like miniature eyes

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Low-growing annual that rarely exceeds 6 inches tall, with delicate branching stems that feel fragile to the touch and often form small colonies

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Small, oval to lance-shaped leaves arranged in opposite pairs along the stem, with smooth edges and a soft, tender texture

idTips.label: Seeds
idTips.description: Produces tiny capsules that split open to release small, dark seeds - shake a mature plant gently and you might hear the seeds rattle inside

habitat: In New England, this rare wildflower is typically found in moist, shaded areas of mountain forests, particularly at higher elevations. Look for it in rich, well-drained soil under the canopy of mixed hardwood and conifer forests, often growing alongside other shade-loving wildflowers and ferns.

seasonality.spring: Plants emerge and begin blooming in late spring, producing their characteristic two-toned flowers on delicate stems. This is the prime time for identification when the distinctive blue and white flowers are most visible.
seasonality.summer: Continues blooming through early summer, with plants reaching their full height and flower production. Seeds begin developing in small capsules as older flowers fade.
seasonality.fall: Plants complete their lifecycle by producing and dispersing seeds from small capsules, then die back completely as an annual species. Look for dried stems with empty seed capsules.
seasonality.winter: No above-ground presence - seeds lie dormant in the soil waiting for spring conditions to germinate and begin the cycle anew.

funFact: This tiny wildflower is incredibly rare in New England with only one documented observation, making it one of the most elusive native plants in the region - you're more likely to spot a moose than find this delicate beauty in New England's forests!
confusionNotes: The two-toned flowers make this species quite distinctive, but it could potentially be confused with other small blue wildflowers from a distance. However, the characteristic split coloring - white upper lip and blue lower lip - is unique among New England's flora and serves as a definitive identifier.
contextualKnowledge: This species was previously classified in the Figwort family (Scrophulariaceae) but has been moved to the Plantain family (Plantaginaceae) based on modern genetic research. The reclassification reflects our evolving understanding of plant relationships, though the plant itself hasn't changed - just our scientific understanding of where it belongs in the family tree.
compareHints: Small-flowered blue-eyed mary is much smaller and more delicate than its western relative Purple Chinese Houses, which has showier, larger flowers and grows taller. While both share the characteristic two-toned flowers of the Collinsia genus, small-flowered blue-eyed mary lives up to its name with blooms that are notably tiny compared to other members of its genus.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Purple Chinese houses differs from its relative small-flowered blue-eyed mary by having much more prominent, colorful flowers arranged in obvious tiers, rather than tiny, inconspicuous blooms.
